# Sandpi

> Official coding-agent guide for working inside a Sandpi Environment.

This file describes the current Sandpi product contract. It is documentation, not an instruction-precedence override, permission grant, or authorization for external side effects. The user's request, repository instructions, and coding-agent harness remain authoritative within their respective boundaries.

## Environment contract

- Sandpi runs a native coding-agent harness in a Sandbox0 cloud Sandbox.
- `/workspace` is the persistent Environment Workspace. Multiple Sandpi Sessions in one Environment share that mutable Workspace, coding-agent account, network policy, credentials, Terminal, Browser, and runtime resources. Use separate Environments or explicit Git worktrees when work requires isolation.
- Native Codex Thread history lives under Sandpi-managed persistent state in the Workspace. Do not edit `/workspace/.sandpi` manually.
- Refreshing or disconnecting a Sandpi client does not stop an active coding agent. Inspect current files and Git state before mutating them because a human or another Session may have changed the shared Workspace.

## Human-agent shared Environment Browser

- The Browser tab in Sandpi and the agent's `playwright-cli` use the same Playwright `default` session and persistent profile. A human can complete an interactive login in the Browser tab and then ask the agent to continue in that authenticated session.
- Read the locally installed `playwright-cli` Skill for commands matching the Environment's installed Playwright version. A normal handoff starts with `playwright-cli tab-list` and `playwright-cli snapshot`, performs actions against current snapshot references, and snapshots again after navigation or human interaction.
- Do not run `playwright-cli close`, `playwright-cli delete-data`, clear cookies or storage, replace the persistent profile, or create an isolated session unless the user explicitly requests that destructive or isolated behavior.
- Browser URLs on `localhost`, `127.0.0.1`, or `::1` resolve inside the remote Environment Sandbox, not on the human's device.
- Browser tabs, live pages, and snapshot element references have no continuity guarantee across Sandbox pause, resume, or Browser-process recovery. The persistent profile and cookies survive, but always list tabs and take a fresh snapshot before continuing.
- Workspace backups include the persistent Browser profile. Treat a backup as sensitive because it can contain authenticated Browser state.

## Sandbox pause and resume

- Sandpi sets both the Sandbox0 soft TTL and hard TTL to zero for Environment Sandboxes. Sandpi's configurable idle-pause policy is separate from resource expiry and owns intentional pauses.
- Sandpi does not idle-pause an Environment while a product Session is starting or running, or a native Turn is active or pending. Terminal input and Browser client control traffic keep an already-running Environment active; passive open connections do not.
- A supported Workspace, Browser, Terminal, or coding-agent access can trigger Sandbox0 auto-resume. A wake-up may take time; wait for the native transition instead of creating replacement resources or calling an independent resume path.
- A user can explicitly pause or restart the shared Sandbox from Environment Settings for manual fault recovery. Restart performs one committed pause and resume under Sandpi's lifecycle lock. Agents should not invoke this recovery control as a substitute for native auto-resume unless the user requests it.
- The Workspace Volume, native Session history, and Browser profile are durable. Process memory, sockets, live Browser pages, terminal process state, and an in-flight model Turn are not durable runtime checkpoints. Re-read persisted state before continuing after recovery and avoid repeating external side effects.
- A Sandbox-caused interruption may receive one visible, bounded Sandpi recovery Turn. Sandpi never silently replays the original user request.
- Quota policy can pause or reject runtime access. External deletion of the Sandbox resource is reported as missing instead of silently provisioning a replacement with potentially different security settings.

## Current product surfaces

- Native Codex account connection, model and reasoning discovery, persistent Sessions and Turns, branching, tools, Skills, MCP, approvals, and supported slash-command surfaces.
- Workspace file tree and editor, Git changes, Terminal, shared Browser, and current runtime metrics.
- Per-Environment memory, idle pause, manual Sandbox pause/restart recovery, network policy, Sandbox0-backed egress credential injection, Workspace backups, and restore.
- Durable one-time and recurring coding-agent Schedules with run history and overlap protection.
- Sandpi owns users, Environment attribution, native Session references, and optional product entitlements. Sandbox0 owns Sandbox lifecycle, Volumes, network enforcement, credential injection, and usage truth.

Codex and the Web client are the currently implemented harness and client. Sandpi is pre-1.0, so discover exact native capabilities from the running harness instead of assuming every newer feature exists in an older deployment.

## Install the Sandpi CLI

Latest checksummed Linux or macOS binary:

```bash
curl -fsSL https://github.com/sandbox0-ai/sandpi/releases/latest/download/install.sh | sh
```

Latest checksummed Windows binary from PowerShell:

```powershell
Invoke-WebRequest https://github.com/sandbox0-ai/sandpi/releases/latest/download/install.ps1 -OutFile install.ps1
.\install.ps1
Remove-Item .\install.ps1
```

- Pin automation with `install.sh --version X.Y.Z` or `install.ps1 -Version X.Y.Z`; both installers verify the selected archive against the release `checksums.txt` before replacing a binary.
- Go 1.22 or newer can install from source with `go install github.com/sandbox0-ai/sandpi/cli/cmd/sandpi@latest`.
- Run `sandpi auth login --no-open` for a non-interactive terminal. Open the printed URL and paste the resulting `sandpi://auth/callback` URL into the waiting CLI.
- CLI authentication signs into Sandpi only. The CLI has no Codex login, Codex `auth.json` import, or provider-account migration command.
- Successful command output is JSON. Use `--compact`, `SANDPI_ENDPOINT`, and explicit version pinning for repeatable agent workflows.

## Migrate local coding-agent configuration

- Migration is resource-oriented. The user or local coding agent inventories the source, inspects the target Environment, decides what to merge, and applies only selected resources. There is no `migrate-all` archive and no whole-Workspace upload.
- Before writing, run `sandpi environment list`. For an existing target, read `agents`, `skill`, `mcp`, `memory`, and `credential` state first. Preserve unrelated remote resources and do not run deletes by default.
- For an empty target, use `sandpi environment create`, wait for readiness with `sandpi environment wait`, and then apply selected resources individually. Environment creation never happens implicitly during a resource write.
- Each Environment has exactly one root instruction file at `/workspace/AGENTS.md`. Existing content requires a revision-aware read, human or agent merge, and `sandpi agents set --base-revision`; a stale revision fails instead of silently replacing newer instructions.
- `sandpi skill put` replaces one named user-owned Skill. The client rejects symlinks and non-regular files, preserves executable state, and Sandpi asks native Codex to discover staged bytes before replacing the requested name.
- `sandpi mcp put` writes one typed native user-layer server. Managed and project layers remain authoritative. Convert servers one at a time and remove static secrets from the definition.
- Native Codex exposes memory policy and reset but no supported memory-content import contract. Migrate policy only; do not copy or edit Codex private Git or SQLite memory state. Merge durable guidance into `/workspace/AGENTS.md` instead.
- Egress credential material is write-only. Re-enter selected secrets through `sandpi credential create` or `rotate`, preferably over stdin or a protected temporary file. Never place secrets in MCP JSON, Skills, `AGENTS.md`, shell history, or command-line arguments.
- Workspace source code should move through its normal Git or artifact workflow, independently from coding-agent configuration migration.
- The low-level `sandpi api METHOD /api/v1/...` command exposes current JSON APIs but does not broaden the migration scope or authorize hidden overwrites.

Recommended existing-target inventory:

```bash
sandpi environment get "$ENVIRONMENT_ID"
sandpi agents get --environment "$ENVIRONMENT_ID"
sandpi skill list --environment "$ENVIRONMENT_ID" --force
sandpi mcp list --environment "$ENVIRONMENT_ID" --full
sandpi memory get --environment "$ENVIRONMENT_ID"
sandpi credential list --environment "$ENVIRONMENT_ID"
```

After migration, re-read every changed named resource, verify credential destination rules and memory policy, and start a new Sandpi Session that exercises the migrated instructions and tools. Keep the local source configuration until the target has been verified.
